items.text: – Vžžž, Baba, Baba, mi kupis to veliko puncko?
items.q: On the street, a stranger's little girl asks her dad for a big doll. Does it sound like baby talk?
before: – Amir, Amir-jan, moj sin. Zbudi se. Zbudi se, mamin. Vse je bilo le sanje. Ne boj se, tu sem.

…prijetno, pomirjujočo temno temo, a ni dajala dovolj svetlobe, da bi me kam povedla. Svetilko, ki pomežikne v roki dekleta, čigar barve vrat nikoli nisem izvedel, čigar barve nikoli nisem uspel umestiti v škatlo lesenih barvic. Deklica pridrvi z »vžž vžž« in se ustavi ob meni. Gleda igrače. Reče:

items.text: Marmalni kamen je. Marmal pomeni zelo drago.
items.q: Ghassem, a boy, says 'Marmal' for marble and thinks it means expensive. Does it read as his childish mistake?
before: Šli smo naprej. Na pol poti je bila hiša. Njena stena je bila lepa. Ghassem je vedno rekel:

items.text: Dež ne pada navzgor iz zemlje. Tudi stari so imeli dobre reke.
items.q: Maman quotes an old saying and says the old folks had good sayings. Does 'dobre reke' mean good sayings here?
before: – Bog ne daj, ne govori tako. Ni otrok tisti, ki naj bo žrtev — ampak mati.

items.text: Pojej glavo mojega kurca, no, nimamo živcev zate.
items.q: Hooman, thumb up, tells a know-it-all to eat the head of his dick. Does 'Pojej glavo mojega kurca' sound natural?
before: Hooman je znova dvignil palec in rekel:

items.text: Ali si možgan-... no, možgan-kurac si bil že, zdaj si pa še bolj možgan-kurac.
items.q: Hooman starts an insult, stops, then makes it worse: dick-brained. Does 'možgan-kurac' work as a crude insult?
before: – Naenkrat si se zafiksiral na to vprašanje. Obstaja več možnosti. Ali si si udaril glavo nekam.

items.text: Ti bedni ... huhhh ... glavo tako dol ... huhhh ... kam greš v takem tempu
items.q: Hooman, out of breath after chasing Amir, calls him a useless prick between gasps. Does this sound natural?
before: Neka roka povleče moje levo ramo nazaj. Je Hooman. Sope.

items.text: Možganadrek, nihče te ne bo imenoval nemega, če ne prdneš.
items.q: Eskandar wakes Amir with a crude twist on an old saying about keeping quiet. Does this sound natural?
before: …na svoji postelji in razmišljal o tem, o čemer sva govorila z Niloofar. Luči na hodniku so ugasnile in hrup iz drugih sob je tudi zaspal. V temi in tišini polnoči je Hoomanova senca vstopila skozi vrata in šla naravnost k škatli sladkic. Kakor da je vohljala. Zjutraj me je Eskandar zbudil in rekel:

items.text: In ti, s tistim tvojim kurčevim načinom govorjenja, bi moral imeti ime Alain Kurčon.
items.q: 'Alain Kurčon' is meant as a rude pun on the actor Alain Delon. Would Slovenian readers get it? If not, what word could carry it?
before: – Da, Hamoun je dobro ime zate. Kakor Hamoun v filmu, si tudi ti poln vprašanj. Poln si tesnobe in si vir nemira, ne zase, temveč zame.

items.text: Človek dobi usrano vrtoglavico. Bolj ko razmišljaš o tem, hujša je ta usrana vrtoglavica.
items.q: A student uses a crude made-up phrase for how a baffling painting scrambles your head. Does this line sound crude like that?
before: – ... poglejte, kako zares vzbuja premislek. To je narisal in pod to zapisal: to ni pipa.

items.q: Maman echoes the ending of 'Ženskar', meaning their father was every other kind of rascal. Would Slovenian readers get it? If not, what word could?

items.text: Oh-ho. Hamid Mačka, včeraj si rekel khar. Zdaj si pa postal civilizirani in praviš osel?
items.q: Taghi teases Hamid: yesterday he used a blunt word for donkey, now he's gone all polite and says 'osel'. Does the jab work?

items.text: Huh. Prijatelj bratranca mojstra našega svaka, ki je najbogatejši človek v Teheranu, govori natanko tako.
items.q: Hamid, a boy, always boasts about a long chain of contacts ending in a rich man. Does this running joke sound natural and funny?
Hooman says sarcastically that the only factory they own is a bullshit factory. Does this sound as crude as he would say it?
before: Eskandar je dvignil glavo s preproge in z velikimi očmi pogledal Hoomana. Hooman je nadaljeval:

items.text: Roka mi je kratka, združitev s tabo pa daleč.
items.q: Amir tells the girl he loves why he holds back. A Persian expression kept word for word: can you guess its meaning?
